The analysis reports between-group contrasts (bvFTD subgroups with vs without altered phobic reactivity) with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected local maxima within predefined ROIs; results are whole-brain voxelwise and clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample (bvFTD group not pooled with other syndromes). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not an excluded modality).

This is an empirical VBM study in PLOS ONE that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=27). This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This study used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13, I4), and had adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20, I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational within a combined patient cohort and significant effects were reported only within pre-specified regions of interest; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are presented, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are reported. This study reports FDG-PET (I3) on a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD; I4). Imaging results are voxelwise SPM whole-brain analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics comparing patient groups to healthy controls (satisfies I6, I7, I8). PET subgroup sizes meet the minimum (H1 N=31, H2 N=10, controls N=16), and whole-brain between-group contrasts (H1 vs controls, H2 vs controls, and H1 vs H2) are reported, with coordinates provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup (n=9) within an FTLD sample of 14 patients, and provides whole-brain voxelwise SPM results in stereotaxic space. However, it does NOT report a between-group contrast of bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) versus healthy controls, and the reported whole-brain results are for a pooled FTLD group (FTD, SD, PPA) compared to an EOAD patient group rather than isolated bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the FTD sample (17 bvFTD patients) satisfying the minimum sample-size requirements (I4, I5), the reported voxelwise whole-brain results are for the pooled FTD group (FTD = 52) and for AD vs controls. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts or coordinate results that are specific to the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup (bvFTD) alone. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and the requirement that at least one whole-brain result be clearly identified as coming from the target sample (I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI and reports voxelwise group comparisons with MNI coordinates. The ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) met clinical Neary criteria for FTD and predominantly showed behavioral abnormalities consistent with bvFTD; neurologic disease controls (n=15) are included. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patient and control groups ≥6). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present; supplementary material being online is acceptable. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that compares a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (behaviorally defined FTD; patients with predominant behavioral/frontal syndrome, excluding progressive aphasia/semantic dementia) to healthy controls using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient sample includes 9 FTD participants and 26 controls, meeting the minimum N≥6 for both groups (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported in stereotactic space (SPM coordinates; e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are presented and attributed to the FTD sample (I6, I7). Results are reported as corrected and uncorrected voxelwise findings and coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC/CTh-only, or prohibited comorbid-sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the inclusion criteria: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient group n=12 and control group n=12, both ≥6), I6 (reports between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported), and I8 (results described in text/figures/tables). This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates bvFTD.
